definitions.explanation: The central and most important part of something. Used in biology for the cell nucleus, in physics for the atomic nucleus, and figuratively for the core member or central element of a group or organization.
Used as a prefix in compound words related to nuclear energy, nuclear weapons, or nuclear science.

examples.japanese: {細胞|さいぼう}の{核|かく}を{観察|かんさつ}する。
{彼|かれ}はチームの{核|かく}となる{選手|せんしゅ}だ。
examples.english: He is a core player on the team.

examples.japanese: この{研究|けんきゅう}グループの{核|かく}となっているのは、{若手|わかて}の{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}たちだ。
examples.english: It is the young researchers who form the core of this research group.

examples.japanese: {核|かく}エネルギーの{利用|りよう}。
{核|かく}{実験|じっけん}に{反対|はんたい}する。
{核|かく}の{脅威|きょうい}は{冷戦|れいせん}{時代|じだい}から{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: The nuclear threat has continued since the Cold War era.

notes:
COMMON COMPOUNDS (sense 2, nuclear):
- {核兵器|かくへいき}: nuclear weapons
- {核実験|かくじっけん}: nuclear test
- {核融合|かくゆうごう}: nuclear fusion
- {核分裂|かくぶんれつ}: nuclear fission
- {核家族|かくかぞく}: nuclear family

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 1, core):
- {核|かく}となる: to serve as the core
- {核|かく}を{成|な}す: to form the nucleus of
- {組織|そしき}の{核|かく}: the core of an organization

USAGE:
{核家族|かくかぞく} (nuclear family) uses {核|かく} in the sense of "core/nucleus" rather than "nuclear weapons," though the English term "nuclear family" has the same etymological origin.
